why: The floors in .github/workflows/ci.yml are a policy: `a floor is 90% of what the job really produces in CI`. A policy with no reading behind it drifts - the floors sat at 64%-87% of the real numbers, so the sentence and the matrix disagreed in the direction that hides a lost face. This file is the reading the floors are derived from. packages/coding-agent/test/ci-floor-policy.test.ts recomputes ceil(floor_ratio * collected/ran) from it and fails when ci.yml (or scripts/lib/ci-process-smoke.mjs) disagrees, so the numbers cannot drift away from the sentence again, and when a row whose floors live in another file stops being recorded in `exceptions` with that file's real numbers.
rounding: ceil - a floor is never below the policy share, and ceil(0.9*6)=6 is why the machine-wide row has no slack

source.command: gh run view 35341768020 -R Dmatut7/prime-agent-rlm --log | grep -E 'numTotalTests=|tests=[0-9]+ ran='
source.why_this_run: Its head sha is the exact commit these floors are committed on, so the readings and the tree being gated are the same tree.
source.log_grep: each row's `log_line` is the gate's own reading line, verbatim from that run's log; packages/coding-agent/test/ci-floor-policy.test.ts re-parses it and fails when it disagrees with the numbers next to it

rows.name: ai
rows.note: 19 nothing-files are the live-provider suites: they need credentials this job has none of, and the budget is exactly 19.

rows.name: tui
rows.note: `node --test`, not vitest: the junit XML feeds check-node-test-coverage.mjs and the budget key is max_nothing_suites.

rows.name: coding-agent 2/3
rows.note: The budget says six kernel-heavy files; this run produced one nothing-file. Left as authored (the budget's semantics are out of scope here) and recorded so the gap is visible: the tight min_ran_tests floor is what catches five more files going quiet.

rows.name: coding-agent process smoke
rows.note: The 12 skips are declared one by one in PROCESS_SMOKE_TAG_SKIP_LEDGER and counted by scripts/check-tag-skip-ledger.sh.

rows.name: coding-agent machine-wide
rows.note: Six tests in one file: ceil(0.9*6) is 6, so this row has no slack at all. Deliberate - it is the machine-wide discovery face and losing a test here must be loud.

rows.name: coding-agent kernel
rows.note: `test:kernel:ci` writes the report and runs the gate itself, so ci.yml carries no floors for this row. At the pinned run it gated at --min-tests 30 --min-ran-tests 29 = 58%/67% of the reading; the policy floors are 47/39. Not changed here: that file belongs to another lane (handed over in REPORT.md).

exceptions.name: coding-agent kernel
exceptions.reason: This row is not gated by ci.yml: `test:kernel:ci` writes the report and runs scripts/check-vitest-coverage.mjs itself, so its floors live in packages/coding-agent/package.json. At the pinned run they are --min-tests 30 --min-ran-tests 29 against 52 collected / 43 ran, i.e. 57.7% / 67.4% - below the 90% policy, and the one place where the policy sentence and the numbers still disagree. The policy floors for this row are --min-tests 47 --min-ran-tests 39. It is a one-line change in that file, left to the lane that owns it so two lanes do not write the same file; packages/coding-agent/test/ci-floor-policy.test.ts fails whenever these recorded numbers stop matching that file, so the gap cannot be forgotten, and it fails the same way once the file is fixed - update this entry then (the exception becomes an ordinary reading).

ungated_rows.name: runtime python
ungated_rows.reason: `uv run python -m unittest discover -s test`: no JSON/junit report, so the only gate is the runner's own exit code. Recorded here so a new matrix row cannot be ungated silently - the pin requires every row to appear either in `rows` or in this list.

cross_check.note: The run the audit quoted. Same readings for every row except the three shards: vitest re-shards by file list, so a shard's own count moves when files are added or removed (shard2 2985->3117, shard3 2176->2058 between this run and the pinned one, total 7869->7895).
The run immediately before the pinned one: every row identical to it, which is why one run is enough to derive the floors.

how_to_refresh: 1. pick a green run: gh run list -R Dmatut7/prime-agent-rlm --branch merge/repl-kernel --limit 5 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion
2. read it: gh run view <run id> -R Dmatut7/prime-agent-rlm --log | grep -E 'numTotalTests=|tests=[0-9]+ ran='
3. per job, print the floors the policy asks for: node scripts/check-vitest-coverage.mjs --recompute-floors <report.json> --row "<matrix row name>"
4. paste the reading into `rows`, the floors into ci.yml (or scripts/lib/ci-process-smoke.mjs for the process smoke row), and update `source`
